$description: The Plenix brand rules (library wave 3, Brand application): how the brand kit's files are applied in the product. Source: plenix-brand-spec.md (the owner's kit). BrandMark (components/Brand) draws them; the brand tokens (tokens/components/brand.tokens.json) hold the sizes and clear space named here, and tests/brand-rules.test.js checks that they agree.

clearSpace.rule: Keep at least 10% of the mark's width clear on every side; nothing else enters it.
clearSpace.mark: The kit's mark square already includes it (56 of 512 units on each side, about 11%): the system adds none around the mark alone.
clearSpace.lockup: A logo, wordmark or product mark that stands on its own (sign-in page, about box, exported document) takes clearSpace: one inset step on the 4px grid, at least 10% of its mark.

minimumSize.rule: The kit tests the mark at 16, 32 and 64 px. Below 16 px the central cross closes: the size scale starts there (sm), so nothing smaller can be asked for.

backgrounds.why: The kit's blue mark on white.
The light blue mark on a dark background: the brand tokens switch with the mode.

backgrounds.surface: The accent (the blue header, an accent banner)
backgrounds.why: The kit's white mark on blue.
The kit's black mark on white: one color, the current text color.

backgrounds.surface: A photograph, a pattern or a busy illustration
backgrounds.why: The mark loses its contrast and its shape.

backgrounds.surface: A status or data color (danger, success, a chart color)
backgrounds.why: The brand is not a status: it competes with the meaning of the color.

misuse: Stretching, rotating, skewing or cropping the mark or the logo
Recoloring the mark outside its tones (brand, mono, on accent), or with a gradient, a shadow or an outline
Redrawing the mark or changing its modules or the 8-unit channel between them
Retyping the wordmark in another face, weight or letter spacing
Placing the mark smaller than 16 px, or crowding its clear space
Using the mark as an action icon, a bullet or a decorative pattern
Inventing a lockup: a tagline, another name or another symbol next to the mark
